disease_label_per_paper: Exertional heat stroke with microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, DIC, MODS, ARDS, AKI, rhabdomyolysis, and myocardial injury
presentation_summary: 25-year-old previously healthy man collapsed 200 m from the finish line of a 5 km training run after 54 minutes in a 28 C and 66% humidity environment.
On-site medical staff recorded highest body temperature 40.3 C, heart rate 140 bpm, and blood pressure 80/50 mmHg; he was unresponsive and received fluids and cooling before local hospital transfer.
After 13 days he was transferred/admitted with ongoing illness after high fever, loss of consciousness, and anuria; arrival vitals were temp 36.8 C, HR 82/min, RR 18/min, BP 156/78 mmHg.

Admission labs included WBC 10.16 x10^9/L, hemoglobin 87 g/L after transfusion, platelets 407 x10^9/L, D-dimer 13273 ng/mL, ALT 264.4 U/L, myoglobin >3000 ng/mL, troponin T 1.1 ng/mL, creatinine 307.2 umol/L, CK 4717 U/L, LDH 265 U/L, CK-MB 69.6 U/L, and pro-BNP 2937 pg/mL.
Day 21 labs showed hemoglobin 64 g/L, ruptured erythrocyte rate 15%, LDH 1213 U/L, haptoglobin <6.63 mg/dL, ferritin 1444 ng/mL, Coombs negative, supporting MAHA.

Final diagnoses included EHS, AKI, acute lung injury, ARDS, DIC/coagulation abnormalities, rhabdomyolysis, acute myocardial injury, moderate anemia, and lactic acidosis; he improved after ICU care, CRRT, mechanical ventilation, and multidisciplinary management.
